hints: Remember what each test is looking for, one test finds carbonyl groups and the other finds a very specific methyl group arrangement.
2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone, so first sort out which of the four contains a C=O group.
The iodoform test gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so check which alcohol can be oxidised to that structure in the test tube.
walkthrough:
**Recall the 2,4-DNPH test**

Think of this as the carbonyl detector. It gives an orange precipitate with aldehydes and ketones only.

Test rule:
$$\text{R-CHO or R-CO-R' + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Recall the iodoform test**

Think of this as the special methyl detector. Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ only with two structures.

Test rule:
$$\text{molecules containing CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{or CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \rightarrow \text{yellow CHI}_3$$

**Apply both tests to the four compounds**

Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) is an aldehyde, so DNPH positive. Propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) is a methyl ketone, so both tests positive. Propan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$) contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so iodoform positive after in situ oxidation.

Only propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) has no C=O and no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so it gives neither precipitate.

options.A: Propanal is an aldehyde, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH because it contains C=O. It does not give iodoform, but the question asks for neither test positive, so this fails.
options.B: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It has no carbonyl group so no reaction with 2,4-DNPH, and it lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$. It is negative to both tests.
options.C: Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It gives no orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH, but it contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. Under the oxidising iodoform conditions it is oxidised to propanone and then gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.D: Propanone is a ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. It gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH, and because it is a methyl ketone ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) it also gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline iodine.
